meta.title: Flagged for review
meta.purpose: Every value that could not be confirmed from an official source, every gap, and every irregularity found while working line by line. Nothing here is hidden in a footnote.
meta.rule_applied: If a value could not be confirmed against an official NFL page, it was left blank and listed here. No value was inferred, estimated or recalled from memory to fill a cell.

flags.title: Clubs have played an unequal number of games
flags.what: In the 2026 standings snapshot, games played range from 8 to 9 across the 32 clubs because of bye weeks and the in-progress Week 10 slate.
flags.why: Per-game rates are still comparable, but raw season totals (PF, PA, wins) are not. Any ranking that mixes totals across clubs with different game counts is wrong.
flags.handling: Ratings are computed per game. The games-played column is published so the user can see the mismatch.
flags.closure: None needed; it is a real property of a mid-season snapshot.

flags.title: Core roster numbers could not be confirmed on an official page
flags.what: Active-roster size, game-day active size, the game-status publication deadline, and the current practice-squad size are all left blank or marked unverified. An Associated Press article surfaced in search describing a 17-man practice squad, which conflicts with the NFL.com report of 16.
flags.why: These numbers set the frame for every availability calculation. Publishing a remembered number as a verified one would be exactly the failure mode this project forbids.
flags.handling: Rules R05, R09, R11 and R12 are marked unverified. R09 carries the conflict note.
flags.closure: Find an official 2026 NFL Football Operations roster-rules page (or the current CBA summary) and quote the four figures directly.

flags.title: Most game statuses did not exist yet at fetch time, and two clubs were not captured
flags.what: Of 108 transcribed injury rows, only 6 carried a game status (Out / Questionable). The remaining 102 were practice-report entries only. Buffalo's report was captured partially and the New York Jets report was not captured at all, because ingestion stopped part-way through the source page.
flags.why: For a Sunday game fetched on a Thursday this is the expected state under the league's own scheme, but it means this week's extract cannot support a start/sit decision on its own. The BUF/NYJ omission is an ingestion limit, not a data property.
flags.handling: Coverage is stated on the Injuries page and in the dataset metadata. No status was inferred from a practice line.
flags.closure: Re-snapshot the same page on Friday and Saturday; complete the BUF and NYJ reports.

flags.title: No NFL-authored odds archive, so nothing can be validated
flags.what: nfl.com/odds/ returns 404. NFL Support confirms that NFL widgets show odds 'provided by official bookmaker partners of the NFL (FanDuel, Caesars, and DraftKings)' and that bets are placed through a redirect to the bookmaker. So odds are visible on NFL surfaces, but they are a partner feed, not an NFL product, and no historical archive is published. Consequently no closing line, CLV, ATS record, backtest or leaderboard score exists anywhere in this project.
flags.why: Lines are supplied by licensed sportsbooks, not authored by the league. This is a structural fact about the source landscape, not a limitation of effort. Anything extracted from a partner widget would be a snapshot of a third party's price, with no guarantee of history or continuity.
flags.handling: Every model output is labelled a model-implied number, never a line. The leaderboard publishes zero scored strategies rather than fabricated ones.
flags.closure: Purchase a historical odds archive (SG-01) and define the closing-line snapshot rule in writing (Q-04).

flags.title: Week 10 slate is only half captured
flags.what: Eight of the sixteen Week 10 games were verified with their dates, kickoff times and networks. The remainder were beyond the truncated portion of the source pages.
flags.why: The model lines therefore cover half a slate. No matchup was invented to fill the gap.
flags.handling: The 8 verified games are published; coverage is stated as 8 of 16.
flags.closure: Fetch the remaining schedule pages or use a full-slate feed.

flags.title: Player-level usage source unverified
flags.what: No official stats surface was fetched, so no claim is made about whether snaps, routes, targets and carries are published there, or at what cost.
flags.why: Every player-prop strategy depends on usage data. Without it, props cannot be originated at all.
flags.handling: All prop strategies are marked BLOCKED at G0 and G10. No prop line is published.
flags.closure: Q-03: fetch and document the official stats surfaces field by field.

flags.title: Legal status of the reward structure unverified
flags.what: No regulatory source was consulted. Whether betting and paying performance rewards is lawful for the operator's jurisdiction is unknown.
flags.why: The project is designed to pay rewards for top-performing strategies. If the underlying activity is not lawful where the operator lives, the reward structure must not be built.
flags.handling: No stakes, no money, and no real-money linkage are implemented anywhere in this build. The site is analysis only.
flags.closure: Q-05: written legal opinion, not a forum post.

flags.title: Depth order (1st/2nd/3rd string) is not in the official roster feed
flags.what: The official NFL.com roster page exposes player, number, position, roster status, height, weight, experience and college. It has no depth-rank column. It was read in full to confirm this.
flags.why: The central requirement — detecting when a 2nd, 3rd or 4th string player must replace a starter — is a depth-order question. Without an order, any 'backup' label would be an invention.
flags.handling: The DepthStress index measures verified availability degradation by position group. It explicitly does not claim who replaces whom, and says so in its own definition.
flags.closure: Q-09 / SG-05: verify per-club official depth charts, or derive order from an official snap-count source, for at least 30 of 32 clubs.

flags.title: No leg-level outcomes, so no correlation coefficient is estimated
flags.what: The only correlations computed in this project are cross-sectional team correlations (C1-C8) from season aggregates. No pairwise leg correlation for parlays or props exists.
flags.why: Parlay and combo pricing depends entirely on the joint distribution. Any rho used would be an assumption dressed as a measurement.
flags.handling: The copula mathematics is implemented and published; every parlay strategy is BLOCKED at G9. The illustrative tables state their parameters explicitly and are marked synthetic.
flags.closure: Q-14: build a leg-level outcome table for at least two seasons and estimate rho per market cluster.

flags.title: 'Questionable' has no measured calibration
flags.what: The definition is verified (uncertain whether the player will play). The actual play rate of players carrying the designation is not measured, and this week's extract has only 6 designated players.
flags.why: If a designation does not predict participation, every model feature built on it is noise. Assuming a probability would be an invented value.
flags.handling: No probability is assigned to any designation. The availability weights used in DepthStress are declared assumptions (A-04), not calibrations.
flags.closure: Q-20 / SG-06: join several seasons of designations to official inactive lists and compute play rates with confidence intervals.
